coverage.authoredAnalysis: Original cover visually read: Modelo de Desarrollo de la España Vaciada, organisation identity and Revuelta logo. Native header version v 9; no 2023 election identity within standing-model cover.
Labordeta epigraph and attribution, not a policy.
Complete contents for introductory organisation, tables 2 reformulation and constitutional/fiscal/EU/energy themes. Page references preserved as source index, not semantic proof.
Complete contents for social care, healthcare, infrastructure, conventional rail and renewables; missing numbered M 3.2.3 is not invented.
Complete contents for renewable generation/connectivity and productive sectors, industry/trade/logistics/tourism/innovation; no mapping from contents headings.
Complete contents for agriculture/forestry/environment and education/university/research/culture; all subheadings and printed references read.
Complete contents for rural enterprise/security/housing/population plus glossary and first bibliography references; national rural housing plan differs from rent ceiling.
Remaining complete bibliography and annex index read, including forest management experiences. Listed references are separate source chains, not read external documents.

Introduction describes territorial depopulation, 2020 coordinated drafting and seven sectoral tables, adequate stable public financing and sustainability. Historical causes/effects are attributed claims.
Plurality, participation, justice, sustainability, transparency and cooperative values, no precise household policy.

Rationale attributes demographic structural crisis to spatially concentrated industrialisation/mechanisation. Analytical background not independently certified factual impacts. Original banner visually read: development-model title and organisation logo only; no hidden policy.
Whole-government territorial response, technology/service/economic transition and 30 provinces/12 regions/140 groups as source organisational claims.

Coordinating membership explicitly includes Jaén Merece Más, SoriaYA, TeruelExiste and others; participation is not automatic adoption by every 2023 ballot. Eight tables/180 participants/82 platforms are author claims.

Entire original visual overview read: framework, reformulation, social cohesion, infrastructure/energy, development engines, primary sector, culture/research, rural opportunities. Diagram labels not present in native extraction retained as visual reading.
Mesa 2 reformulation and Mesa 4 infrastructure/connectivity rationale; diagnosis and claimed thesis findings are source arguments, not guaranteed policy consequences.
Continues infrastructure rationale; economic diversification/talent and comparable rural public services/housing. General quality goal supplies no specific dental/free-price entitlement.
Rural self-image, community empowerment and sustainable primary resources; claimed effects remain attributed. No hunting/animal-policy stance from sustainability alone.
Complete objectives, holistic planning and EU rural-proofing/fiscal support for low-density areas; less 12.5 inhabitants/km 2 and 2019 amendments are source frame rather than verified current law.
Conclusions urge comprehensive national/regional rural strategy, employment/services, two-vector declining-population/low-density diagnosis. No individual quiz-policy values inferred.
Continues diversified economy/talent and tailored response to every affected rural community; empty objections heading does not prove consensus.
Mesa 2 divider title and surrounding page read; no additional native policy.

Mesa 2 overview links government levels, State pact, strategic agrifood/forestry, independent national depopulation agency and inclusive youth return. Institutional aspirations distinct from enactments.

Overview continues 100/30/30/local financing/rural taxation/green compensation/article 138/rural guarantee/EUcomarcal scope/renewable employment and landscape; all conditions retained for later substantive-page reading.

Finishes renewable-territory compensation; table 2 objectives include long-term cooperation, rural legislative differentiation and public services within 30 minutes. No low-fare transport mechanism is supplied.

Rural resident/enterprise incentives, economic diversification, rural-proofing, EUfund criteria, green-tax compensation and gender perspective; no universal tax relief inferred from territorial differentiation.

Women equality/youthreturn and national/European independent depopulation agencies; structural political independence alongside democratic local participation, not complete transfer of decision power to technicians.

Finishes institution autonomy; State pact adopted with broad parliamentary support. Demographic catastrophe statistics/predictions are source assertions; Article 174 quoted as rationale, no automatic current-law verification.

State-pact objectives explicitly include 1% of GDP annually, an autonomous agency, Law 45/2007 funding, gender equality, a rural guarantee and implementation of equality, dependency and shared-farm legislation. This 1% is not the defence-spending proposition.
Stable annual 1% GDPfinance, OECD/Cork/SmartVillages references; public autonomous audited agency with participation and consulting; rural-gender statistics are unverified source data.

Continues source statistics on gender, wages, management, employment and domestic work. Both original graphs were fully read: sex/total distribution by work hierarchy and pay bands, attributed to the rural-development directorate. No numerical policy score or six-month leave entitlement follows.

Rural-women legal implementation, specific law, agency parity and exantegenderimpact requiring positive corrections; complete oversight indicators/audits/sanctions. A broad law reference does not establish individual provisions.
Strategic agrifood/forestry classification with national sovereignty/food self-supply and rural comparable services; source pandemic/effect claims distinguished from proposals.

Strategic sectors: traditional local markets, minimum production-cost catalogue, local seasonal trade/direct sales, smallfarms/cooperatives. Specific producerprice floor is not a residential rent ceiling.

Promotes extensive livestock and sustainable technical forestry; limits intensive mega-farms. Proposes a production-cost floor, free digital-skills courses and agricultural-policy payments only to farmers paying agricultural contributions, with youth aid. No general hunting ban.
Depopulation-agency rationale invokes ScotlandHIE, institutional independence and multiyear investment. Comparative success/percentage/causal claims not verified; not promises of effects in Spain.

Immediate objectives for an independent public agency: comparable rural services, entrepreneurship and individual administrative advice, stable budgets, public audit portal, parity and citizen participation. Advice does not explicitly authorise intermediary filing.

Public employment and contracting rules apply to the agency; administrations retain strategic direction. Territorial delegations cover at most one million residents, with headquarters outside cities exceeding 100,000 residents and with functional centres. State and regional powers require cooperation.

Agency leadership election and gradual renewal, project promotion, research and European-grant advice, audited stable public budget. Begins inclusive youth-return rationale; demographic statistics remain attributed.

Youth return targets people up to age 36, including vulnerable people and flexible residence evidence; available public housing in each village, 5 G, technical services within 30 km and cultural access. The overview says youth immigration while later text says emigration; retain the discrepancy.

Return-plan eligibility extends up to age 36 with at least two years outside the province; accepts multiple residence-evidence options and extensions for vulnerable youth. Integrated simultaneous measures and general student support do not specify tuition prices.

Agency youth office and evaluation every six months; aim to reach 25% in two years and 50% in five years. Research contracts last at least three years; young returners receive a self-employment fee exemption or subsidy for the first two years. Vulnerable-young-person social rent and first-year return housing aid are limited measures.

Young-returner first-home transfer-tax exemption and agency guarantee, internal-migration criteria, youth train/bus discounts and telework travel relief. Nurseries, vulnerable-family aid and rural schools with four or more pupils, with flexible reopening. Neither universal free 0-3 provision nor a first-home VAT exemption is specified.

100/30/30 rationale cites constitutional article 139, infrastructure studies and the 2019 document. Healthcare, death and causal claims are not independently verified. Its referenced annex differs from the Jaén programme emergency map.

100 Mbps symmetric connectivity throughout rural and urban territory; services within 30 minutes, highway/rail within 30 km and at least one weekly in-person primary-care visit in every municipality. Intermediate 50% coverage in 2022 and full coverage in 2025 are historical model deadlines.

Continues 2025 connectivity responsibilities; services within 30 minutes through administrative comarcas, a mesh network, distributed facilities/professionals and accessible daily public mobility. Specialist/social-centre distance requirements and mobile community services.

Mobile libraries, high-capacity road access within 30 km, overdue transport-plan works, new mesh corridors and an accessible-transport plan. Public/social mixed passenger-freight conventional rail and study of closed lines. No short-flight restriction.

Local and comarca financing rationale invokes EU article 174, constitutional article 138 and municipal autonomy under article 140. Source legal descriptions are not verified law or a Congress constituency reform.

Local Services 30 funds, subprovincial demarcations, cooperative networks, a technical grants office and demographic/socioeconomic distribution criteria. Institutional grant advice is not individual representative filing.

Density and population-loss priorities with a national consultative commission, SEPES rural industrial funds and study of greater use of municipal reserves. Services 30 comarca framework must respect local autonomy and existing municipal associations.

Services 30 allocates 30% of its budget through participation: 10% to services, 10% to municipal cooperation and 10% to associations. Shared heritage teams and a technical office address local grant eligibility and policy advice; this is not a household benefit.

Finishes municipal resources, management and cooperation rationale; begins differentiated rural taxation across income, corporate and value-added taxes. Neither inflation indexation nor a first-home VAT exemption is established.
Full affirmative-action rationale and footnote references read; comparative historical/legal assertions attributed. No new concrete tax instrument on this page.
Continues equality/constitutional solidarity and rural relocation tax rationale; corporate and social-security incentives stated as goals, claimed effects unverified.

Employment incentives: small municipality, minimum 70% nearby resident workers and distance criteria; contribution rebates 80%/70%/60% by population and sex, plus 4% remote increment continued. Not universal zero fees.

Further under 5000 population/70% resident criteria and 40%/50% rebates;15% corporate tax-quota deduction for qualifying establishment; effective residence proof; alternative 50% tax-to-loan repayment requires prior request and is incompatible with earlier benefits.

Any-location existing firms qualifying 30% rural workers get 30%/20% contribution rebates, plus 5% under 36 relocation; investment reserve 90% qualifying profit for low-density territories must generate jobs and fund defined capital uses.

Reinvestment within 2 years, traceable local branch profit and self-employed extension; local contribution rebates 40-60%;3 yeartelework relocation after 1 yearaway supports housing/under 3 care/training. Rural income-tax deductions 15-25% plus dependants and bounded local-spending deduction; under 1000 rental-income exemption.

Inheritance relief only under 1000 resident heirs and qualifying local real estate; property-transfer exemption conditional on productive use/rehabilitation;4% VATrural primary goods and named services. No nationwide family inheritance exemption or firsthomeVATzero.
Green-tax rationale/earmarking for rural environmental stewardship, pollution disincentives and climate commitments; fiscal comparisons/claimed environmental effects remain source assertions.

Progressive green levies on extraction, mega renewables, intensive farms, waste and damaging pesticide/fertilizer use, earmarked for affected territories. Paying tax does not exempt environmental compliance; levy is distinct from product prohibition.

Public/private environmental stewardship incentives and territorial earmarking, including carbon sinks, self-generation and energy renovation. Repeated incomplete sentence retained; no named utility-disconnection ban.

Completes coordinated green fiscal rationale; begins constitutional solidarity/territorial balance justification with legal and scholar references. These are publisher interpretations, not verified legal guidance.
Constitutional articles 40/131/158/156/138 and case-law cited for investment/solidarity; full footnote attribution read. No proposed Congress constituency change.
Continues EU solidarity reference, then interior/coastal economic and demographic imbalance diagnosis. Comparative claims/table introduction are unverified source background.

Complete 2019 regional surface/population/GDP table read, including group exclusions and Madrid, Canarias and Ceuta distinctions. Original table visually checked for column groupings and geographic exclusions. Source figures are not promoted as independently established facts.
Melilla/totals and sourceINE 2019 continuation, percentage interpretation and positive-discrimination objectives. Alternative population percentages differ from table, not silently reconciled.
Express proposal to add depopulation consideration to article 138 while maintaining territorial solidarity/insular protection. Broad legal change distinct from all provision-specific policies.
Full proposed article 138 text read, including privilege constraint; begins ordinary-law differentiated rural legislation rationale and external affirmative-action attribution.
Continues full differentiated-legislation rationale, including reverse-discrimination objections and uniform-rule adaptability. Normative argument not a released policy position.
Rural statutory differentiation rationale covers deficient services, small markets, women employment and simpler urban structure. Diagnoses are attributed, without forecasts used as quiz premises.
Objectives of adapting laws and positive treatment for residency and entrepreneurship; generic service quality does not specify individual price or access entitlements.

Public subsidies prioritize social service value; rural housing rehabilitation and tailored urban planning retain necessary controls; equality measures for rural women. No permanent public housing ownership duty.

Sectoral public employee reform: rural effective residence, difficulty-zone points, supplements, training and three-year interim continuity or preferential replacement list. No doctor retirement age policy.

Continues employee housing/training; rural public procurement preference under residence and contract-location conditions. Entire article 145 footnote read; proposed amendment distinguished from existing text.

Full proposed social-contract criteria and kinship incompatibility removal for small rural tenders; local SME/cooperative preference. Full continued footnote includes after-sales/spare-part criteria, not a general repair-parts mandate.
Continues minor-contract eligibility and proposed rural urban-planning/land-rule simplification; ruin expropriation only after procedure, notice twice and owner failure to rehabilitate.

Unknown-owner property assigned locally only after investigation/no-owner declaration; inventory public property; rural primary school three-pupil minimum conflicts with four-pupil passage 42. Rural women law begins.

Women-law measures: equality plans over 500 residents, gender clauses, municipal ballot parity above 1000,40% decision positions in agrifood bodies, shared farming and care support; no Congress ballot reform inferred.

Violence-victim shelters, flexible work/school reconciliation without age 16 entitlement; administrative-site decentralisation and rural business bond-finance law. Rural-proofing begins with Cork rationale.
Complete Cork recommendations, reported parliamentary nonbinding motion and constitutional 131/138 text. Source legal history not independently verified or confused with enacted guarantees.
Constitutional 139 and motion continuation; objectives require rural legislative/budget impact review before 2023, EU tools, technical training and local participation. Historical deadline retained.
Rural guarantee designed with all government levels/civil society/local groups/experts; evidence reports, independent agency application and ongoing technical/political training.
EU low-density definition rationale cites treaty cohesion and calls for precise causal/situation indicators. No standalone domestic rights position from treaty quotation.
Classification using density plus cumulative decline, births/deaths, ageing and masculinity; targets equitable effective EU fund distribution. No invented numeric cutoff here.
Low-density European register using subprovincial units; begins reforming cohesion programs with complete treaty 175 quotation and parliamentary interpretation.
Aggregated geography can hide needy areas; prioritize depopulation and comarcas as fund recipients with distributed local development. Claimed EU effects attributed.
Comarca municipal autonomy/cultural ties; provincial criteria until defined;2021-2027 cohesion priority for low-density areas alongside funding criteria. Period-specific proposal retained.
INTERREG low-density priority, research/training decentralisation, European agency auditing national agency and European depopulation day; begins renewable just-transition theme.
Renewable siting compatibility with employment/landscape/agriculture/tourism; claimed 95% job-loss figure is background, not independently verified.
Alternative decent local jobs, renewable siting in low-landscape-value/distant areas with local deliberation/referendum; agrivoltaic diversification and individual/cooperative self-generation.

Cooperative surplus paid at least market price; local participation up to 25%, land/tax/development compensation and free energy for residents/enterprises in generating territory, producer-funded. Not universal vulnerable-household direct aid.

Company community obligations, producer-consumer energy funds and carbon-source/sink redistribution; consider summer-time retention. Compensation mechanisms differ from renewable prohibition or nuclear lifetime policy.
Original social-cohesion table 3 divider visually read; decorative puzzle graphic only.
Social-cohesion background identifies rural diversity, vulnerability, connectivity and employment/housing as prerequisites. Broad adequate services do not establish every specific quiz entitlement.
Children/youth/women/older people/disability/minority groups and dignified pensions; pensions adequate does not specify cost-of-living indexation.
Universal publicly funded free healthcare principles quoted from law; claimed staffing/management deterioration attributed. Broad legal citation alone does not establish expanded dental care.
Professional healthcare-management qualification scheme; explicitly phase out copays for pensioners and other vulnerable groups. Narrow eligibility must not become universal copay abolition.
Veterinary participation in public health and equal social/health opportunities, disease assertions unverified; begins childhood/youth community inclusion.

Education/social/health coordination, psychopedagogic and family teams, rural environment teaching, low-cost anti-child-poverty and sport/culture activities. No exact physical-education hours or pandemic tutoring target.

Continues rural recreation network; education technology subsidies where necessary for vulnerable families, not universal free internet. Dependency-law rural equality and coordinated close services begin.

Dependency resources and multidisciplinary person-centred care; caregiver temporary absence from work, support and respite programs. No immediate ALS-diagnosis recognition or fixed benefit appointment deadline.
Continues respite, then elderly rights/legal pension sufficiency and active ageing. Quoted periodic pension update lacks a stated price-index formula.

Active-ageing participation/home care; dignified pensions tied to increasing living standards, internet training, accessible transport/banking and in-person basic healthcare. Living-standard wording does not automatically mean price indexation.
Nearby public residences/home ageing support; disability accessibility rationale with UN/CERMI assertions and transport barriers, attributed rather than independently certified.

National disability inclusion strategy, municipal universal accessibility, employment/education, early care, transport and local services within 30 minutes. Early-care price/public operator not specified here.

Employment target of 20% in five years, individual guidance and SME hiring. Disabled rural residents receive a self-employment fee exemption for three years, then a reduction up to 50% under the stated income condition. No blanket fee exemption.

Early-care centre in each comarca within 30 minutes, continuity after the transfer at age six and year-round availability. Accessible buses/taxis and subsidised demand transport for disability needs. General eligibility, destinations and fares remain unresolved.
Disability participation/training and intersectional social inclusion for migrants, gender-violence victims,LGTBIQ+andRoma groups; general accessible demand-responsive transport goal.
Migrants language instruction, civic participation, legal advice and dignified jobs; language attendance linked to benefits. No general administrative representative filing established.
Migrant housing/training/legal support, labour inspection and trafficking prevention; gender-violence health/social/police coordination, nearby psychological therapy and legal advice.
Violence prevention/training/housing/jobs and safe rural reintegration; victim-specific psychological support not universal public psychotherapy expansion. Begins sexual-diversity inclusion.
LGTBIQ+ school support and anti-bullying protocols, social educators and free anti-discrimination legal advice; begins Roma background. No surrogacy or abortion policy.
Roma education/employment/participation and women inclusion; literacy, early schooling, attendance support and professional anti-discrimination training. No 0-3 freeentitlement.
Roma employment/rights/family advice and housing plus community support; holistic settlement-policy rationale begins. Advice distinct from formal administrative delegation.
Settlement utilities quality: local renewables, participatory-energy studies, water inspection and asbestos-pipe removal. Quality guarantees differ from nonpayment disconnection protection.
Wastewater projects/connectivity coverage and sufficient social housing/emergency reserve/abandoned-building reuse. Neither universal freeinternet nor perpetual publichousingownership.

Cultural/community spaces and subsidised demand-responsive trips with accessible vehicles; nearby public 0-3 centres and school transport for ages 0-18. Public provision does not establish zero price.

Homecare substitutes/basic neighbourhood supply and multidisciplinary social centres including possible psychologists; illustrative service possibilities not guaranteed universal psychotherapy entitlement.

Complete illustrative social-centre catalogue read: free electronic-administration access, advice, internet, coworking, libraries, recreation and mobile services. Free administrative access is not universal basic home internet.
Home-centred elderly care with temporary small residences and public-preferred investment/operation; higher dependency requires other nearby suitable resources, not indefinite home-only guarantee.

Inclusive accessible community spaces; phased local/returning/other-user eligibility and partially autonomous disability extension; daily ancillary services and publicly financed or soft-loan housing adaptations.

Public accessibility upgrades/local staff/occupational activity/energy communities; care services should be public but private concessions allowed with oversight; auxiliary services mostly private. No healthcare-agreements position inferred.
Cooperative user cofinancing and the full external-example bibliography; clinical-history access across regions through information systems. Referenced external reports are separate unread sources.
Rural primary-care rationale about staffing/workload/training/retention and family medicine. Staffing forecasts/causes attributed; no doctor age 72 extension.

Primary-care budget of 25%, staffing, coordination and services; pensioner/disability copay removal, weekly in-person clinic, rejection of telephone triage, more residency-training places and long-term contracts. No guarantee of completing all administrative procedures in person.

Completes training; health centres attract specialists including psychology/dentistry, maintain equipment, compensate travel costs and establish nearest-service agreements across regions. Price and entitlement scope need exact-rubric review.
Interregional regularisation; localclinic funded maintenance/uniform equipment/accessibility and weekly inpersonappointments; most-demanded specialist decentralisation begins.

Specialists within 30 minutes, agreements across regions and study of companion travel-cost support; urgent transport within 30-minute catchments, adapted vehicles and coordination of conventional/community transport.

Limits nonmedical vehicles; night-capable medical helicopters and safe helipads. Health-centre equipment includes dentist/hygienist facilities, physiotherapy, diagnostics and emergency equipment. Clinical and safety efficacy assertions are not certified.

Equipment funding and accessibility; compensation for private rural pharmacies providing a public-interest service and reliable electronic-prescription connectivity. No public pharmaceutical manufacturing company.
Original infrastructure/energy table 4 divider visually read; transport imagery is decorative.

Road/rail/renewable/connectivity diagnosis and historical radial network rationale from 1761/1926. Historical causal assertions are publisher claims. Original complete page checked; native text and headings cover all nondecorative content.

1926 and 1950 road-plan maps/captions and radial-network critique. Both historical originals read, including special-surface circuit, modernisation plan and radial/subradial/peripheral/complementary legends. Tiny incidental labels are not evidence.

1968-72 road-plan caption and 1984-91 motorway narrative. Original REDIA 1967-1971 map read with year-colour legend; historical radial-road illustration. Caption/map date difference retained; no current-road guarantee.

1984-91 map, discontinuity after 1993 and 2012-24 transport-plan critique. Original motorway-programme map read with in-service, first-phase and second-phase legends. Claimed political causes are attributed.

Planned high-capacity road map and reported A-23 isolated areas of 80,631/50,505/30,126 km². Original national/autonomous/study-connection legend and island insets read. Source access-area claims remain unverified.

A-23 area map, radial investment/development claims and preference for a territorial mesh over new Madrid rings. Original network map read with 50,505 and 30,126 km² marked areas and transport-horizon legend.
Original 2018 heavy-traffic map read with Madrid-area annotation, alongside planning critique. The MITMA paradigm diagram is on page 139; source mobility claims are attributed.

Stable maintenance investment versus construction; source employment multipliers and post-Covid quotation. Original MITMA diagram read: infrastructure provision versus mobility policies, old deficit investment versus climate/urbanisation/digitalisation needs. Background diagram does not supply a policy score.
Completes post-Covid quotation and ministry references; goals of network mesh, maintenance, safe access and transport investment. No transport-price or flight-restriction stance.

Execute pending PITVI works, provide high-capacity access within 30 km across the territory, mesh corridors, broad consensus and shorter administrative project times. Empty objective fields are not supplemented.
Prefer local presence for road-project and works contracting; prioritise local and provincial works and stable ordinary conservation contracts.
Retain decentralised conservation staff and centres and locally managed small works; urgent pavement rehabilitation and scenic roads.
Accessible national transport plan; historical conventional rail and high-speed comparison, track gauges and competitiveness claims attributed to the source.
Renew conventional rail to 160/200 km/h, improve stations and access, rolling stock and freight workshops and the railway industry.
Conventional rail agenda and reopening socially useful lines; mixed public passenger/freight mesh, source unit 25 KW retained, polyvalent sleepers and UIC ambitions.
Safety and intermodality, 750 m sidings, reversible closed-line law, sufficient public-service frequencies, new rolling stock and local industry; comfortable stations and platforms.
Accessible real-time arrival information, comparable or reduced ticket prices where rail is the sole transport, combined tickets without price penalty, staff retention and onboard assistance.
Renew railway workforce, study closed-line feasibility and maintain conventional services; renewable-energy rationale begins.
Distinguish renewable, clean and sustainable energy; just, ecological, decentralised and democratic transition. Energy-poverty safeguards do not specify a nonpayment disconnection ban.
Local stable employment, efficient buildings, accessible smart meters, fiscal incentives and penalties, energy-management department; distributed sustainable renewables and solar theme begins.
Prefer local self-consumption; surplus levy, solar workforce at least 60% local where possible and 15% of production value to a provincial employment fund; integrate landscapes and agriculture.
Simple self-generation and community rules; recover or create small hydro in secondary channels, not main-river barriers. No public-management rule at concession expiry.
Sustainable forest and agricultural waste, compost before energy, 12,000-ton/year local pellet threshold and larger-plant footprint; avoid crop biofuels. Biomass impact claims remain attributed.
Sustainable urban and building rules, local and reused materials, climate adaptation, efficiency, self-generation and reasonable costs.
Continues material, waste and planning rules; wind installations up to 10 MW, repower existing parks and penalise inefficiency.
Wind workforce 60% local and 15% production-value fund, small community generators; green hydrogen replacing fossil transport fuels.
Sustainable public and individual mobility; anaerobic biogas with toxicity and environmental conditions, renewable research and community evacuation networks.
Distributed electrical network; rural connectivity and pandemic rationale, Plan 300 x 100 and PEBA history. Source incorrectly calls Mbps megabytes; preserve the unit ambiguity.
Broadband deficiency and report reference plus a referenced telecom-transversality report; digital skills, telework and business infrastructure. External report not included or read.
Basic broadband access goal by 2025; use dark fibre along high-voltage lines, railways and roads. Referenced Reintel Teruel map is an unread external item.
Proposed telecom-law amendment allowing local licensed-spectrum use without fees where one or no operator exists; repeater and own-network exception; rural PEBA plan begins.

Community, small-operator and municipal networks where major firms are absent; territorial coverage priority; penalties for unexecuted grant projects and avoid impossible small-operator tender requirements.
Digital agriculture, telework and rural public services require connectivity; mandate broadband for official and service centres and complementary public projects without overlap.

Connect health centres, municipalities, pharmacies, social services and police; technology does not replace territorial police presence. Broadband in every settlement regardless of size, avoiding excessive installation charges and exploring alternative finance.
Coworking, coliving and multiservice centres can serve as fibre distribution nodes, rural innovation spaces and banking-service hubs.
Original productive-sector table 5 divider visually read; decorative gears only.
COVID-era production and employment diagnosis and historic investment claims; short-term recovery focus on SMEs, commerce, industry and tourism. Forecasts are historical source assertions.
Defensive crisis support, liquidity and preservation of firms and vulnerable groups; medium-term modernisation and competitiveness. No universal income or blanket tax measure inferred.
Digital literacy, renewables, national sector finance and industrial-share target of 20% GDP; sustainable tourism and unified promotion. Jura watchmaking example is attributed background.

Talent, organisation and infrastructure networks; avoid tax increases where possible during crisis, encourage investment and saving, then fiscal consolidation mainly via public-spending moderation and efficiency.

Continue fiscal differentiation; simplify regulation, retain prior-crisis structural reforms where possible, labour flexibility and arbitration. Wording that reforms do not work adequately is internally awkward; no exact labour-dismissal proposition established. Rural industry begins.
Diversified community and cooperative industry with possible public investment, green production and rural innovation; income and population-retention objectives are source claims.

Community employment over personal or speculative enrichment, local transformation and distribution, circular economy and rural research; participatory territorial master plans with periodic revision.

Locally financed proactive commercial office with activity indicators. Tax, land, one-stop-shop and export measures explicitly deferred to later model revisions; renewable industrial self-use proposed.

Local renewable land/tax support; low-interest, long-term loans for efficient irrigation, renewable power and predictive technology. Local processing from farm to consumer with training and fewer intermediaries.

Circular local packaging and rural-product quality seal; advanced cooperatives for research and commercialisation, local administrative support. Claimed emission savings not independently established.

Local vocational/university curricula, return of emigrated talent, dual training and adult education; full list of potential production sectors read, including food, batteries, crafts and forest products.

Proximity-commerce and post-pandemic consumption rationale; two proposed channels are discounted consumption vouchers and social-income vouchers. Renta básica heading does not imply universal unconditional income.
Illustrative €50 voucher bought for €40, public €10 contribution; scalable according to annual public budgets. Claimed benefits are advocacy rather than guaranteed effects.
Gijón social-income pilot and claimed ODS impacts, amounts and satisfaction; refers to Annex M 5.1. Case-study evidence is not a universal entitlement.

Social-income voucher eligibility: insufficient income, adult applicant, one-year registration, Spanish nationality or regularised foreign status and provincial criteria. Stores must join, operate locally, register activity and have IT access. Original UN Sustainable Development Goals grid visually read with all 17 labels; contextual illustration does not add an entitlement.
Entire municipal voucher amount/population/per-capita table read; source labels figures own compilation subject to change. Statistics do not score a policy.

Business digitalisation introduction with attributed pandemic e-commerce and internet statistics; original graphic content must be checked. Original Digital around the world January 2020 graphic read: population 7.75 billion/55% urban, mobile 5.19/67%, internet 4.54/59%, social-media 3.80/49%, We Are Social/Hootsuite attribution; historical descriptive data only.
Local direct-sale marketplace without seller cost, producer-set prices, digital marketing and omnichannel strategy; first business-support module covers idea, viability and finance.
Business grants, incorporation and one-stop-shop assistance; rural quality seal criteria, brand and full sale-channel classifications.
Sales administration, payments, invoices, tax help and costs; digitalisation grants, affordable telecom agreements and SME training. No general zero-price residential internet.

Individual external digital mentoring and university collaboration; eight areas including search, social media, online commerce and AI; indicators and fiscal attraction rationale. Original commerce-digitalisation diagram visually read: commerce linked to Big Data/AI, design/video, social media, SEO, SEM, online commerce and omnichannel; no new independent measure.
Internationalisation and logistics objectives; identify corridors, dry ports and production hubs, including reuse of underused airports and rail infrastructure.
Industrial logistics areas with public access works and freight airports; sustainable tourism begins with attributed COVID-era GDP and employment data.
Unified tourism inventory, sustainable local employment, longer stays, training and rules for novel tourism activities; minimum seven-day stays are an objective, not a legal visitor obligation.
Thematic circuits, local-food links, certain tourist-site access fees, grants, guide training and hospitality schools. Claimed benefits are source expectations.
Linked comarca tourism offices, web inventory, signage reform, open cultural resources, grants and discounted rural lodging vouchers; local/regional implementation.
Events and congress tourism, incoming travel agencies, long-stay packages and preference statistics; enterprise knowledge-economy section begins.
Rural business networks, talent, public procurement access, university links, diversification and simple business administration; joint purchasing centre.

Responsible declarations and one-stop-shop; rural/local procurement clauses, business cooperation, second chances and supported retirement-transfer schemes. Coworking expressly charges symbolic rent, not free access.
Digital worker retraining; decentralised tech-production rationale, lower local costs and renewable-adjacent data centres; claimed competitiveness not independently proven.

Business sites, education partnerships, dual training and graduate hiring subsidies; stable return-talent recruitment. Differentiated rural fiscal and labour policy begins, subject to European recognition.
Regional fiscal advantages, productive investment and credit, sustainable diversification and retaining ERTE mechanisms independently of emergency status. Separate August 2019 document referenced.

Public-backed, no-cost participatory loans with declared viability; regional tax relief for territorially eligible residents and property. Source confusingly pairs transfer-tax label with net-worth rationale; do not correct or score it silently.

Income deduction requires prior geographic depopulation zoning; rural social-contribution rebates, guarantees, entrepreneur aid and faster public payments. Entire original fiscal table read: regional/state resident income relief, wealth/transfer/stamp-duty/inheritance relief and company-profit relief tied to local fiscal residence. No universal abolition.
Agroindustry and forest/fire support, provincial funds, unused land/buildings, wage subsidies and more independent/resourced tax inspection. Demographic indicators introduce graphic content.

Demographic citation and relocated elderly-care section. Entire original 2018 Spain/Aragon/Teruel table read: population change/density, age/gender/birth and municipality-size indicators, attributed to IAEST/INE through the Teruel document.
Source states no objections; this does not certify external agreement or remove earlier internal ambiguities.
Original primary-sector table 6 divider visually read; decorative crop image only.
EU rural-demographic diagnosis and consultation rationale; primary production as rural-development engine. Historical causes and predicted effects are attributed.
Complete primary-sector objectives: sustainability, innovation, PAC reform, organic/proximity production, women, professional training, local processing and cultural heritage.

Rural-proofing and Cork principles; agriculture/stockraising bureaucracy, slow geographical-certification processes, falling farm prices and insufficient origin/method labelling. Simplification and faster certification objectives.

Comarca one-stop-shop and generational renewal; strengthen food-chain law to prevent sale below production cost and improve origin/method labelling. Agricultural model introduction criticises nonlocal/transgenic seeds.
